methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Virginia's AI challenge isn't data centers. It's small-business adoption | Guest column - Richmond Times-Dispatch
signals.signal_reading: Richmond Times-Dispatch op-ed explicitly identifies the concentration paradox: Virginia's AI infrastructure wealth in NoVA contrasts with weak small-business adoption statewide, signaling shallow distributed capability even as deep expertise concentrates in data center corridors.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents intentional capability-building infrastructure outside traditional tech hubs, creating potential distributed deep learning if the lab cultivates peer networks beyond campus rather than simply credentialing individuals.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops in Hampton Roads signal grassroots capability distribution through peer learning networks, explicitly framed as closing technology gaps—a direct counter to concentration if sustained beyond individual events into ongoing communities of practice.

signals.title: Appalachian Power sees ‘explosive’ growth from data centers, other big customers
signals.signal_reading: Appalachian Power's 'explosive' data center growth in historically underserved Southwest/Southside creates infrastructure concentration without guaranteed capability distribution—physical proximity to AI infrastructure doesn't automatically translate to local workforce depth or business adoption.

signals.title: Google to invest millions for Virginia workforce development amid data center growth - WRIC ABC 8News
signals.signal_reading: Google's workforce development investment tied to data center growth likely produces platform-mediated training for operational roles rather than deep AI capability—broad but shallow distribution optimized for infrastructure support, not indigenous innovation capacity.
